extracted.intended_audience: users of PARI/GP (computational number theorists, mathematicians, and developers using the PARI library)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of PARI/GP library functions for algebraic number field computations: preconditions, parameter meanings, return formats, limitations, and usage examples for each API routine. Useful for writing scripts, debugging errors, and choosing appropriate routines and flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrstark
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the ray class field using Stark units (bnrstark(bnr)). Main variable of bnr must not be x; ground field and class field must be totally real. When base field is Q, galoissubcyclo is used instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May return a vector of polynomials defining independent relative extensions whose compositum is the requested class field (user must take compositum). Requires finding a suitable auxiliary conductor which may not exist when the class field is not cyclic over the base; conductor may be too large making computation infeasible; Stark's conjecture may be false. In case of difficulties, try rnfkummer. Library syntax: GEN bnrstark(GEN bnr, GEN subgroup = NULL, long prec). Examples and error message shown when computation impossible due to huge intermediate size.

rubrics_metrics.name: dirzetak
rubrics_metrics.description: dirzetak(nf, b): returns the first b coefficients of the Dedekind zeta function of the number field nf as a Dirichlet series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN dirzetak(GEN nf, GEN b). No flags described.

rubrics_metrics.name: factornf (polfnf)
rubrics_metrics.description: factornf(x, t): factorization of univariate polynomial x over the number field defined by polynomial t (Trager's trick reduces to factorization over Q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: x may have coefficients in Q or in the number field. Main variable of t must have lower priority than that of x (see Section 2.5.3). If non-rational number field elements occur as coefficients of x (polmods or polynomials), the variable of these polmods must be the same as the main variable of t. Direct approach using nffactor (van Hoeij's method in relative setting) is generally faster. Example error messages: inconsistent data in rnf function; incorrect variable in rnf function. Library syntax: GEN polfnf(GEN x, GEN t).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisexport
rubrics_metrics.description: galoisexport(gal, {flag}): export underlying permutation group of a Galois group (from galoisinit) as a string suitable for GAP (flag=0 or omitted) or Magma (flag=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows exporting to GAP to compute IdGroup. Accepts subgroups returned by galoissubgroups. Library syntax: GEN galoisexport(GEN gal, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisfixedfield
rubrics_metrics.description: galoisfixedfield(gal, perm, {flag}, {v = y}): compute fixed field of gal by automorphism(s) defined by perm (an element, vector of elements, or subgroup from galoissubgroups). Output is squarefree modulo gal.p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0 (or omitted): return [P,x] polynomial P defining fixed field and x a root expressed as polmod in gal.pol. flag=1: return P only. flag=2: return [P,x,F] where F is factorization of gal.pol over the field defined by P; v is variable number whose priority must be less than that of gal.pol. Example shows returning polynomial and factorization; library syntax: GEN galoisfixedfield(GEN gal, GEN perm, long flag, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisgetpol
rubrics_metrics.description: galoisgetpol(a, {b}, {s}): query galpol package for a polynomial with Galois group isomorphic to GAP4(a,b), totally real if s=1 (default) and totally complex if s=2; returns [pol, den].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: pol is polynomial of degree a; den is denominator for nfgaloisconj(pol) and can be passed to galoisinit or nfgaloisconj to speed them up. If b and s omitted, returns number of isomorphism classes of groups of order a. Library syntax: GEN galoisgetpol(long a, long b, long s). Also available: GEN galoisnbpol(long a) when b and s omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisidentify
rubrics_metrics.description: galoisidentify(gal): output isomorphism class of underlying abstract group as [o,i] where o is group order and i is index in GAP4 Small Group library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts subgroups returned by galoissubgroups. Implementation limited to degree ≤127 with some larger 'easy' orders supported. Output similar to GAP4 IdGroup. Library syntax: GEN galoisidentify(GEN gal).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisinit
rubrics_metrics.description: galoisinit(pol, {den}): compute Galois group and necessary information for computing fixed fields of Galois extension K/Q where K is number field defined by pol. Extension must be Galois with Galois group 'weakly' super-solvable; returns 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Weakly' super-solvable defined: normal series with cyclic quotients and final quotient either trivial or isomorphic to A4 or S4. Practically almost all small groups are WKSS except listed exceptions. Function is prerequisite for many galois routines. If den present, must be suitable for gal[5]. Output is 8-component vector gal with detailed contents (pol, [p,e,q], roots, inverse Vandermonde*gal[5], gal[5] multiple of l.c.d. of automorphism coefficients, gal.group permutation representations, gal.gen generators, gal.orders relative orders). Properties/constraints on gal.orders and generator behavior described. Library syntax: GEN galoisinit(GEN pol, GEN den = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisisabelian
rubrics_metrics.description: galoisisabelian(gal, {flag = 0}): return 0 if gal not abelian; if flag=0 return HNF matrix of gal over gal.gen, if flag=1 return 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts subgroups returned by galoissubgroups. Library syntax: GEN galoisisabelian(GEN gal, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisisnormal
rubrics_metrics.description: galoisisnormal(gal, subgrp): return 1 if subgrp is normal subgroup of gal, else 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: gal from galoisinit, subgrp from galoissubgroups. Accepts subgroups returned by galoissubgroups. Library syntax: long galoisisnormal(GEN gal, GEN subgrp).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoispermtopol
rubrics_metrics.description: galoispermtopol(gal, perm): return polynomial defining the Galois automorphism associated with permutation perm of gal.roots (as output by nfgaloisconj).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: perm can be element, vector, or matrix (applied recursively). For G = galoisinit(pol), galoispermtopol(G, G[6])~ is equivalent to nfgaloisconj(pol) if degree(pol) ≥ 2. Library syntax: GEN galoispermtopol(GEN gal, GEN perm).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoissubcyclo
rubrics_metrics.description: galoissubcyclo(N, H, {fl = 0}, {v}): compute subextension of Q(ζ_n) fixed by subgroup H ⊂ (Z/nZ)^*. N may be integer n, output of znstar(n), or output of bnrinit(bnfinit(y), m, 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation of N & H differs by form of N (integer, znstar output, bnrinit output); when module's infinite place not dividing module, H understood relative to N and may be subgroup of quotient by {±1}. fl=0 compute polynomial in variable v (variable number) defining subfield; fl=1 compute only conductor (module); fl=2 return [pol, N] both. Example polsubcyclo function given to compute all subfields. Library syntax: GEN galoissubcyclo(GEN N, GEN H = NULL, long fl, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoissubfields
rubrics_metrics.description: galoissubfields(G, {flags = 0}, {v}): output all subfields of Galois group G as vector (applies galoisfixedfield to all subgroups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flags meaning same as for galoisfixedfield; v is variable number. Library syntax: GEN galoissubfields(GEN G, long flags, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoissubgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: galoissubgroups(G): outputs all subgroups of Galois group gal as vectors [gen, orders] where gen are permutation generators and orders are relative orders; cardinal of subgroup is product of relative orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such subgroup can be used in galoisisabelian, galoissubgroups, galoisexport and galoisidentify. To get fixed field of subgroup sub, use galoisfixedfield(gal, sub[1]). Library syntax: GEN galoissubgroups(GEN G).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealadd
rubrics_metrics.description: idealadd(nf, x, y): sum of two ideals x and y in number field nf; result given in HNF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show idealadd(K,2,x+1) returns ideal generated by 2 and 1+i. Cannot be used to add arbitrary Z-modules; arguments assumed ideals. For adding arbitrary Z-modules use mathnf(concat(A,B)). Library syntax: GEN idealadd(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealaddtoone
rubrics_metrics.description: idealaddtoone(nf, x, {y}): given two coprime integral ideals x and y (any form), returns [a,b] with a∈x, b∈y and a+b=1. Alternative syntax idealaddtoone(nf, v) where v is vector of ideals summing to ZK; returns vector e with e[i] ∈ x[i] and sum e[i] = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealaddtoone0(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealappr
rubrics_metrics.description: idealappr(nf, x, {flag = 0}): given a fractional ideal x, returns an element α in nf such that valuations match: for primes where val(x)≠0, vp(α)=vp(x); for others vp(α)≥0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag non-zero, x must be prime ideal factorization (output of idealfactor) possibly with zero or negative exponents; returns α with valuations equal to given exponents and vp(α)≥0 elsewhere. Algorithm differs between flags so idealappr(nf, idealfactor(nf,x)) may not equal idealappr(nf,x,1). Library syntax: GEN idealappr0(GEN nf, GEN x, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: ide alchinese
rubrics_metrics.description: idealchinese(nf, x, y): x is a prime ideal factorization (2x2 matrix: prime ideals & exponents), y is vector of elements indexed by ideals in x; computes b such that vp(b - y_p) ≥ vp(x) for primes in x and vp(b) ≥ 0 for all other p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealchinese(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealcoprime
rubrics_metrics.description: idealcoprime(nf, x, y): given integral ideals x and y in nf, returns β in field such that β·x is an integral ideal coprime to y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealcoprime(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealdiv
rubrics_metrics.description: idealdiv(nf, x, y, {flag = 0}): quotient x·y^{-1} of ideals in nf; result in HNF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag non-zero, quotient is assumed integral ideal which can be much faster when norm of quotient small; available variants: idealdiv (flag=0), idealdivexact (flag=1). Library syntax: GEN idealdiv0(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealfactor
rubrics_metrics.description: idealfactor(nf, x): factor ideal x into prime ideal powers in number field nf; output format similar to factor with prime ideals represented in idealprimedec format (5-element vectors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealfactor(GEN nf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealfactorback
rubrics_metrics.description: idealfactorback(nf, f, {e}, {flag = 0}): reconstruct ideal from factorization f; integer 1 corresponds to empty factorization. If e present, product of f[i]^{e[i]}. If f vector and e omitted, e interpreted as vector of 1s. f can be regular factorization output by idealfactor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag non-zero perform ideal reductions (idealred) along the way—useful for extended ideals. Examples show transforming to extended ideals and recovering standard form via nffactorback. Library syntax: GEN idealfactorback(GEN nf, GEN f, GEN e = NULL, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealfrobenius
rubrics_metrics.description: idealfrobenius(nf, gal, pr): assuming K/Q is Galois with gal = galoisinit(nf) and pr is a prime ideal in prid format unramified, returns permutation of gal.group equal to Frobenius element associated to pr (σ(x) ≡ x^p mod P where p is unique prime in P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows 101 ≡ 8 mod 31 giving x^8. Library syntax: GEN idealfrobenius(GEN nf, GEN gal, GEN pr).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealhnf
rubrics_metrics.description: idealhnf(nf, u, {v}): gives Hermite normal form of ideal uZK + vZK where u and v are elements of field K; if b omitted returns HNF of ideal defined by u which may be algebraic number, maximal ideal or matrix of generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If strictly less than N=[K:Q] generators, u is ZK-module generated; if N or more given, assumed Z-basis of ideal (acts as mathnf). Special handling for quadratic fields allowing u = Qfb(a,b,c) with discriminant condition. Examples and an error for Qfb with wrong discriminant shown. Library syntax: GEN idealhnf0(GEN nf, GEN u, GEN v = NULL). Also GEN idealhnf(GEN nf, GEN a).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealintersect
rubrics_metrics.description: idealintersect(nf, A, B): intersection of ideals A and B in nf; result in HNF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not apply to general Z-modules since arguments replaced by ideals they generate. A helper ZM_intersect(A,B) is provided to intersect Z-modules given by matrices: compute integer kernel and use mathnf. Library syntax: GEN idealintersect(GEN nf, GEN A, GEN B).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealinv
rubrics_metrics.description: idealinv(nf, x): inverse of ideal x in nf, given in HNF. For extended ideals [I,t], principal part updated to [I^{-1},1/t].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealinv(GEN nf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: ideallist
rubrics_metrics.description: ideallist(nf, bound, {flag = 4}): compute list of all ideals of norm ≤ bound in nf, result is row vector with bound components; each component is row vector with information depending on flag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag meanings: 0: give bid without generators; 1: include generators; 2: nf must be bnf with units; output [bid, U] where U vector of discrete logs of units (for bnrclassnolist/bnrdisclist); 3: as 2 but include generators; 4: give only HNF of ideal. Examples show usage and how to inspect components and mod structures. Library syntax: GEN ideallist0(GEN nf, long bound, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: ideallistarch
rubrics_metrics.description: ideallistarch(nf, list, arch): given output list from ideallist with flag 0..3, returns vector of vectors with same number of components but with Archimedean part arch added to moduli; leaves give similar information as input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows adding real infinite places modifies class groups (adds copies of Z/2Z). Typical application: combine with bnrclassnolist to get class groups with units. Library syntax: GEN ideallistarch(GEN nf, GEN list, GEN arch).

rubrics_metrics.name: ideallog
rubrics_metrics.description: ideallog(nf, x, bid): computes discrete logarithm of element x (not necessarily integral) relative to generators in bid.gen; bid as output by idealstar(nf, D, ...). x must have valuation 0 at all prime ideals in support of D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result is column vector (xi) with 0 ≤ xi < di where di are orders of generators gi satisfying x ≡ ∏ g_i^{x_i} (mod *D). When D contains infinite places, congruence implies sign conditions on real embeddings. Limitations of discrete log algorithms referenced in znlog. Library syntax: GEN ideallog(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN bid).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealmin
rubrics_metrics.description: idealmin(nf, ix, {vdir}): (deprecated/backward compatibility) computes a pseudo-minimum of ideal x in direction vdir; recommends using idealred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: vdir best omitted; vdir should be nf.r1 + nf.r2 component vector of non-negative integers; library syntax: GEN idealmin(GEN nf, GEN ix, GEN vdir = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealmul
rubrics_metrics.description: idealmul(nf, x, y, {flag = 0}): multiply ideals x and y in nf; result is ideal product in HNF; extended ideals update principal part appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show extended ideal handling. If flag non-zero, reduce result using idealred. Library syntax: GEN idealmul0(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y, long flag). Also GEN idealmul (flag=0) and GEN idealmulred (flag ≠ 0).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealnorm
rubrics_metrics.description: idealnorm(nf, x): compute norm of ideal x in nf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealnorm(GEN nf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealnumden
rubrics_metrics.description: idealnumden(nf, x): return [A,B] where A,B are coprime integer ideals such that x = A/B in nf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: idealnumden(nf, (x+1)/2) returns numerator and denominator ideals. Library syntax: GEN idealnumden(GEN nf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: ideapow
rubrics_metrics.description: idealpow(nf, x, k, {flag = 0}): compute k-th power of ideal x (k ∈ Z); extended ideal principal part updated accordingly ([I,t]^k => [I^k, t^k]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag non-zero reduce during binary powering using idealred which is not same as idealpow followed by reduction. Variants: idealpow (flag=0), idealpows (k long), idealpowred for flag=1. Library syntax: GEN idealpow0(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN k, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealprimedec
rubrics_metrics.description: idealprimedec(nf, p): compute prime ideal decomposition of prime number p in number field K (nf); returns vector of prid structures each representing a prime ideal above p in nf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: pr = [p, a, e, f, mb] where a algebraic integer with valuation 1 at prime, e ramification index, f residue degree, mb multiplication table used to compute valuations; components accessed via member functions pr.p, pr.e, pr.f, pr.gen. Examples show decompositions and retrieving generators/uniformizers. If p non-prime result undefined. Library syntax: GEN idealprimedec(GEN nf, GEN p).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealprincipalunits
rubrics_metrics.description: idealprincipalunits(nf, pr, k): given prime ideal pr in idealprimedec format, returns multiplicative group (1+pr)/(1+pr^k) as abelian group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faster than idealstar when norm of pr large since avoids residue field multiplicative group work. Example shows structure and generators; Library syntax: GEN idealprincipalunits(GEN nf, GEN pr, long k).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealramgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: idealramgroups(nf, gal, pr): for Galois extension K/Q with gal=galoisinit(nf) and pr a prime ideal, return vector g of subgroups: g[1] decomposition group of P, g[2] G0(P) inertia group, and for i≥2 g[i] = G_{i-2}(P) higher ramification groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length of g equals number of non-trivial groups in sequence (0 if e=1 and f=1, 1 if f>1 and e=1). Cardinality of subgroup computed from its relative orders. Examples show computing cardinalities and using returned subgroup in galoisfixedfield to check ramification. Library syntax: GEN idealramgroups(GEN nf, GEN gal, GEN pr).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealred
rubrics_metrics.description: idealred(nf, I, {v = 0}): LLL reduction of ideal I in nf along direction v; finds a 'small' a ∈ I and returns HNF of reduced ideal J = rI/a where r rational making J integral and primitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: v parameter is nf.r1 + nf.r2 component vector of non-negative integers (relative magnitudes matter); usually omit v. If input extended ideal [I,s], output [J, sa/r] preserves principal part. Useful quick test for principality but not conclusive (bnfisprincipal recommended for guaranteed results). Technical note: uses LLL on lattice with quadratic form ||·||_v (rescaled/rounded variant used in practice). Library syntax: GEN idealred0(GEN nf, GEN I, GEN v = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealstar
rubrics_metrics.description: idealstar(nf, I, {flag = 1}): output bid structure necessary to compute in finite abelian group G = (ZK/I)^*. I is a modulus (ideal or [ideal, arch-vector]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: bid contains bid.mod (modulus), bid.clgp (group structure), bid.no (order), bid.cyc (elementary divisors), bid.gen (generators). flag=1 default returns bid without generators; flag=2 include generators (slower); flag=0 return only group as [h,d,g]. Recommended to use Idealstar with OR-ed nf_GEN (include generators) and nf_INIT (return full bid) constants rather than numeric flags for flexibility. Library syntax: GEN idealstar0(GEN nf, GEN I, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealtwoelt
rubrics_metrics.description: idealtwoelt(nf, x, {a}): compute two-element representation of ideal x as x = aZK + αZK combining randomized search and approximation theorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When called idealtwoelt(nf,x) returns [a, α] where a chosen as positive generator of x ∩ Z unless x principal (then possibly a=0); algorithm uses fast lazy factorization and randomized polynomial time. When called idealtwoelt(nf,x,a) with explicit non-zero a (assumed a∈x) returns α∈x with x = aZK + αZK; factoring a slows algorithm. Library syntax: GEN idealtwoelt0(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN a = NULL). Also idealtwoelt and idealtwoelt2 variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealval
rubrics_metrics.description: idealval(nf, x, pr): give valuation of ideal x at prime ideal pr (pr in idealprimedec format).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long idealval(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN pr).

rubrics_metrics.name: matalgtobasis
rubrics_metrics.description: matalgtobasis(nf, x): apply nfalgtobasis to each entry of vector or matrix x (convert algebraic numbers to coordinates on integral basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: nf is nfinit format; x row/column vector or matrix. Library syntax: GEN matalgtobasis(GEN nf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matbasistoalg
rubrics_metrics.description: matbasistoalg(nf, x): apply nfbasistoalg to each entry of vector or matrix x (convert basis coordinates to algebraic numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: nf is nfinit format; x row/column vector or matrix. Library syntax: GEN matbasistoalg(GEN nf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: modreverse
rubrics_metrics.description: modreverse(z): given z = Mod(A,T) polmod and Q minimal polynomial of z with deg(Q)=deg(T), return reverse polmod Mod(B,Q) which is a root of T (a 'reverse polmod').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to change generating element of algebraic extensions and obtain explicit isomorphisms between different defining polynomials. Example shows converting cubic field defined by x^3 - x -1 to another polynomial. If minimal polynomial of z has lower degree than expected routine fails with domain error. Library syntax: GEN modreverse(GEN z).

rubrics_metrics.name: newtonpoly
rubrics_metrics.description: newtonpoly(x, p): returns vector of slopes of Newton polygon of polynomial x with respect to prime p; slopes in decreasing order; vertical slopes denoted by LONG_MAX when constant coefficient zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of components equals degree of x; LONG_MAX corresponds to vertical slopes (machine-dependent max int). Library syntax: GEN newtonpoly(GEN x, GEN p).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfalgtobasis (algtobasis)
rubrics_metrics.description: nfalgtobasis(nf, x): transform algebraic number x in number field nf to column vector on integral basis nf.zk (coordinates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inverse of nfbasistoalg. Examples given. Library syntax: GEN algtobasis(GEN nf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfbasis
rubrics_metrics.description: nfbasis(T): given irreducible integral polynomial T(X) return an integral basis (Z-basis of maximal order) of number field defined by T, elements given in Q[X]/(T).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses modified round 4 algorithm due to Ford, Pauli and Roblot. Supports local basis and orders maximal at certain primes. Library syntax: GEN nfbasis(GEN T).
